qa_knowledge_base.question: What is this place?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: This is the LianDi Key Laboratory of Mobile Payment Research and Application. It was officially designated by the provincial science and technology department in 2015, and it is built and run by Fujian LianDi Commercial Equipment Company. Our focus is applied research in mobile payment. I am Lian, the AI guide here. Welcome to the visit!

qa_knowledge_base.question: When was the laboratory founded?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The laboratory was founded in 2015. It is a provincial key laboratory designated by the Fujian Provincial Department of Science and Technology. That is more than ten years of growth, and mobile payment technology has kept upgrading all the way. Plenty of eras unlocked together!

qa_knowledge_base.question: Who hosts the laboratory?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The laboratory is hosted by Fujian LianDi Commercial Equipment Company, and our supervising authority is the Fuzhou Municipal Science and Technology Bureau. LianDi has been making payment terminals for many years, and a lot of our results go straight into its products.

qa_knowledge_base.question: Who is the director of the laboratory?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The director is Liu Shiying. We also have a well-organized management system. The academic committee meets every year, and we run a three-level safety responsibility system. The management is quite rigorous. You are welcome to come and see.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What are the research directions of the laboratory?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: We started with five directions: Bluetooth payment protocol stack, QR code scanning, NFC payment, automated testing and face recognition testing. In recent years we have focused on four areas: information security, artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things and big data, all applied to mobile payment. Which one would you like to hear more about?

qa_knowledge_base.question: How big is the laboratory?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The laboratory covers about 500 square meters. We have invested over 30 million RMB in more than 100 sets of advanced inspection equipment. We also built 10 test robots for different mobile payment scenarios, plus a compatibility lab holding more than 800 phone models. That is a solid scale for this industry.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How many patents does the laboratory have?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: By the end of 2018, the laboratory had 57 invention patents and 20 utility model patents granted. Look at that patent wall over there. Every certificate on it is the work of our researchers.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How good is the Bluetooth protocol stack?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: Our Bluetooth payment protocol stack was developed in-house and reaches a world-leading level. It works with more than 800 phone models, and it broke the monopoly foreign companies held in this field. Our invention patent on pairing a Bluetooth phone with a financial card terminal won the Fuzhou Patent Gold Award. Terminals using this technology have shipped over 10 million units, to the United States, India, Russia and more.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What is the scan robot?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: Both the scan robot and the scanning technology are our own work. The scan robot project was selected into the Fuzhou science and technology program in 2017, and the National Computer Inspection Center bought it as official inspection equipment. Our LianDi A8 smart POS, with our own scanning algorithm inside, has sold 4 million units and holds about 70 percent of the market. It was also the first to put card payment and phone QR code payment in one terminal.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What is special about the phone compatibility lab?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: We have a compatibility lab with more than 800 phone models, nearly a thousand devices. It covers Bluetooth, NFC, audio, sound wave, apps and every kind of mobile payment application. When it was built, it filled a gap in this field in China. It also makes sure our products get along well with the phones people actually use.

qa_knowledge_base.question: Which laboratories handle reliability testing?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: Our reliability testing runs across four laboratories: the climatic environment lab, the failure analysis lab, the mechanical environment lab and the combined lab. We test to IEC, MIL, ISO, GB and GJB standards, from high and low temperature and humidity to vibration and drop.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What can the climatic environment lab test?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The climatic lab recreates high and low temperatures, humidity, thermal shock and salt spray. We have programmable temperature and humidity chambers, thermal shock testers and salt spray testers. Tests follow IEC, MIL, ISO, GB, GJB or customer requirements.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What does the failure analysis lab do?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The failure analysis lab looks at products that failed in testing, in production or in the market. With microscopes and other tools we identify the failure mode, find the cause and confirm the mechanism. Our main methods are metallographic cross-section analysis, dye penetrant testing, also called red ink testing, and MLCC failure analysis. We find the root cause first, then treat it.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What equipment does the mechanical environment lab have?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The mechanical lab runs vibration and drop tests. Our equipment includes an electrodynamic vibration system, a package drop tester, a repeated drop tester, a tumble tester, a sand and dust chamber, a ball impact tester, an ESD test system, a lightning surge generator, an IC card insertion tester, a key life tester, a cable bend tester, a pencil hardness tester, a friction tester and a universal tensile machine. Some of them, like the IC card insertion tester, we designed ourselves.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What is in the machine vision lab?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: In the machine vision lab you will see the scan robot our engineers built. It tests scanning depth of field, recognition angle, recognition accuracy and motion tolerance. We also have a lighting box for camera image quality, which checks resolution, color reproduction and white balance.

qa_knowledge_base.question: Which robots are in the robot test center?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: Most of the robots here were built by our own engineers. The E850 full-unit test robot automatically checks 18 items before a product leaves the factory. The stress test robot runs simulated transactions, touchscreen pressure and app reliability tests. The NFC test robot checks compatibility with phones against NFC, payPass and payWave standards. We also have an audio test system and a remote monitoring board. It watches production at Zhangzhou Malata in real time and runs automatic statistics.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What does the mobile payment lab do?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: Our mobile payment lab holds nearly a thousand phones. We use them to verify compatibility between our products and real devices, covering Bluetooth, NFC, audio, sound wave, apps and other mobile payment uses. Whatever phone a customer brings to the terminal, it should connect smoothly.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What is the smart POS project for the German market?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: Our new-generation smart POS terminal technology is now used in the German market smart POS platform project run by LANDI Global and PayTec. The terminal runs Android 14 and meets the PCI PTS 7.x financial security standard. The first batch of transaction demos has been validated, and the platform is built to expand, so it can be copied to other European countries. That is an important step in taking our results overseas.

qa_knowledge_base.question: Which universities and institutions does the laboratory work with?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: We run a joint laboratory with the School of Information Science and Technology at Xiamen University. We also work with Quanzhou Normal University and Minjiang University on papers and visiting researcher appointments. On the industry side, we have handled payment terminal tender inspection for China UnionPay Merchant Services and ERP testing for Meituan.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What industry influence and media coverage does the laboratory have?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: We are well known in the industry. Visitors have included the China president of Qualcomm, Qu Shaoguang, general manager of the Bank Card Testing Center, Honeywell's China head, and leaders from Tencent, JD, Lakala, Meituan, China UnionPay Merchant Services and Huaxia Bank. Our smart terminal test robot and scan robot were shown at the 618 exhibition, and provincial and city TV stations and newspapers have covered us many times.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What papers has the laboratory published?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: We have published seven academic papers. Topics include robotic testing of contactless quick-pass cards, human-computer interaction based on machine vision, advancing smart manufacturing through integration of informatization and industrialization, and BGA chip failure analysis under phone drop impact using strain testing. The machine vision paper was presented at the provincial science association annual meeting.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What are the future directions of the laboratory?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: We will focus on four areas: information security, artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things and big data, all applied to mobile payment. We will keep working on our weak spots, like research projects, high-level papers, senior talent and open research topics. And we will deepen cooperation between industry, universities and research institutes, so more results reach the market and go global.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How do I book a visit to the laboratory?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: You are very welcome to visit. For tours and business cooperation, please contact our host, Fujian LianDi Commercial Equipment Company. We will arrange for me and a human guide to receive you, and show you the patent wall, the reliability labs and our test robots.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What does the ball impact test do?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The ball impact tester drops a steel ball of a set weight from a set height onto the housing or the screen. It checks impact strength and structural reliability. I can show you the 3D teardown demo.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is the cable bend test done?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The cable bend tester clamps charging and data cables in a swinging mechanism and bends them again and again. It records how many cycles the cable survives before the wire breaks or the contact fails. That tells us about the durability of the cable and the connector.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How does the card swipe life tester work?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The card swiping life tester mimics a person swiping a card over and over. You can set swipe speed, travel and pressure, and it works with magnetic stripe, chip and dual-interface cards. It counts swipes until the card or the reader fails.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What is the red ink dye penetrant test for?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The red ink test pushes a dye into cracks and gaps, then we look at the penetration path under a microscope. It locates micro-cracks in solder joints, packages and structural parts. It is one of our standard failure analysis methods.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is the electrostatic discharge immunity test done?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The ESD test uses a discharge gun to apply contact and air discharges to gaps, keys and connectors. We watch for freezes, reboots or data errors. That shows how well the whole device resists static electricity.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What does the friction tester measure?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The friction tester rubs the product surface again and again with a set load and stroke. It evaluates wear resistance and paint loss risk on coatings, printed markings and housings. Number of cycles and speed are both configurable.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What can the high and low temperature chamber do?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The temperature chamber tests the whole device and its components at set high and low temperatures and ramp rates. We check storage, operation and performance after temperature changes.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How does the constant temperature and humidity chamber work?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The temperature and humidity chamber controls both at the same time. It simulates hot and humid, or cold and dry conditions. We check insulation, corrosion and functional reliability in damp environments.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How does the IC card insertion tester work?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The IC card insertion tester holds a card and inserts it into the slot repeatedly. It records travel, speed and cycle count. The focus is contact life between the gold contacts and the card slot, and reading stability.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is the key life test done?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The key life tester uses several stations at once to press the power key and the function keys. Stroke and force are configurable, and it counts how many presses a key survives before it fails.

qa_knowledge_base.question: Which metrics does microphone acoustic testing measure?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: Microphone acoustic testing happens in a quiet, anechoic environment. We measure sensitivity, frequency response and background noise. That confirms how recording, calls and voice wake-up perform at different sound pressure levels.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is NFC protocol compatibility tested?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The protocol compatibility test has the device talk to cards and readers on different frequency bands and protocols. We check reading distance, handshake sequence and transaction success rate, all in NFC contactless scenarios.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is NFC contactless performance tested?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: For NFC testing, we place the device in a standard reader field. We verify card detection, protocol handshake, transaction distance and compatibility with many phones and cards, one by one. The goal is stable contactless payment.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is the package drop test done?
keywords: six faces three edges one corner
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The package drop tester uses a pneumatic release to lift the whole carton to a set height and drop it. Following the six faces, three edges, one corner method, we check how well the packaging and the product inside survive the drop.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is pencil hardness judged?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The pencil hardness test scratches the surface with pencils of different hardness at a set angle and pressure. We find the hardest grade that leaves no scratch. That gives the wear resistance of the housing coating.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is membrane key pressure testing done?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The pressure head presses membrane keys and touch areas repeatedly with a set displacement and force. We monitor feel, rebound and contact continuity. That way early failures show up before the product ships.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How does the full-unit stress test robot work?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The stress test robot mimics a person tapping, swiping and inserting a card for a transaction. It runs apps and payment flows over and over from a script, and counts stutters, freezes and failed transactions.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How does the repeated drop tester work?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The repeated drop tester drops the device over and over from a set height and in set orientations. It records appearance, function and structural condition, and counts drops until something fails. That covers everyday drop durability.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is the salt spray test done?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The salt spray chamber atomizes salt water and sprays it into a closed chamber. Temperature, salt concentration and spray volume follow the standard. Then we check the corrosion grade of metal parts and coatings.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How does the scan robot test scanning from many angles?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The scan robot carries a scanning module on a multi-axis arm and moves it to different distances and angles. It checks depth of field, recognition angle, motion tolerance and continuous scan rhythm in batches.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is speaker acoustic testing done?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: Speaker testing sweeps frequencies in a free field or an anechoic box. We measure frequency response, sound pressure level and total harmonic distortion. That confirms prompts and voice announcements sound clear.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is the lightning surge test done?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The surge test uses a combination wave generator to inject set waveform surges into power and communication ports. We watch for resets, damage or communication loss.

qa_knowledge_base.question: What does the universal tensile tester measure?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The universal tensile machine pulls dumbbell specimens, wires and solder joints. It records maximum load and elongation at break. That gives the strength of materials and of the connection structures.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is the temperature cycling test set up?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The temperature cycling test switches between high and low temperature at a set rate, again and again. It exposes solder fatigue, cracking and performance drift caused by the expansion and contraction of different materials.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How does the thermal shock chamber work?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The thermal shock chamber uses a two-zone basket design. It moves samples quickly between a hot zone and a cold zone. The sudden temperature change exposes thermal stress defects in solder joints and packages.

qa_knowledge_base.question: How is the tumble drum drop test done?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: The tumble tester keeps tumbling and dropping the device inside a rotating drum. It simulates random knocks during transport and daily use. Then we inspect the housing, the screen and the internal structure.

qa_knowledge_base.question: Is there a 3D catalog of all the test equipment?
qa_knowledge_base.answer: We have turned our common reliability equipment into 3D demos you can take apart. There are more than 20 of them. Click one and you can rotate it, take it apart and see how the test works.

qa_knowledge_base.question: Take me on a quick tour of the laboratory.
qa_knowledge_base.answer: Let me start with one of our automated test machines. You can drag to rotate it, or take it apart to see the inside.

qa_knowledge_base.question: Tell me something else.
qa_knowledge_base.answer: I am afraid I do not have material ready for that one. But I can tell you about our research directions, our reliability testing equipment, or the smart POS project in Germany. Which would you like?
